questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Canada?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Canada article.

questions.proof: The national capital is Ottawa, and the nation's most populous city is Toronto.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Canada?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Canada on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Canada article.

questions.proof: Most of the people in Canada live in urban areas, near the southern border with the United States.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Canada?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Canada article.

questions.proof: That means that citizens have the right to communicate with the government in two languages: English or French.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1535, two Aboriginal youths told an explorer from _____, named Jacques Cartier, about the route to Kanata.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “named”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Canada article.

questions.proof: In 1535, two Aboriginal youths told an explorer from France, named Jacques Cartier, about the route to Kanata.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is the world's second-largest country by total area, behind _____, but only the fourth-largest country by land area.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “behind”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Canada article, under the heading “Geography and climate”.

questions.proof: Canada is the second-largest country in the world by total area, after Russia.
